title: Studio: a contributed navigation entry shows its id, not its label, and a package that only contributes navigation reads "no app yet"
body:
domain:ui#4 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jR7ZFkpqmm4U8S1f9y

Filing gate: ① user-visible gaps with named locations, class b. These are out-of-scope findings 1 and 2 from the #29786 os-dev report (comment 6597892264, PR #29847), measured live by its dev on `app-multi-package` plus a temporary contributor package. Filed by `domain:ui#4` · ⛔ Not a claim.
reach: every Studio base that another package adds navigation to, and every package whose only navigation is contributed to another package's app.
type: enhancement

**Business reason.** After #29786, a base's Interfaces tree shows each contributed navigation entry greyed with its package. The entry is drawn by its id (`nav_orders`, `nav_acme_portal`), not by the label the person sees in the live app, so the tree and the app read differently. The contributing package's own Interfaces pillar still says "This package has no app yet", although its entries appear in another package's app.

## What happens (after PR #29847)

1. **Id, not label.** `GET /api/v1/packages/:id/customizations` `contributions` `nav` entries carry `app`, `group`, `name` (the nav item's id) and `packageId`. There is no label (`packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts`, the `nav` arm). Per the ruling, the row draws the id. The dev measured that the app list read the Interfaces pillar already makes (`GET /meta/app?package=`) serves the folded navigation, labels included, for the same app.
2. **Contributor side.** A package whose only navigation is a `navigationContributions` entry reads "This package has no app yet." in its own Interfaces pillar. Its package-list row carries the raw `manifest.navigationContributions`, which is the declaration, not the served fold, so #29786 left the text as it was (seat ruling, amendment 6595791720).

## Wanted

1. **Decide where the label comes from, then draw it.** One option: look the label up by `(app, id)` in the served folded navigation the pillar already reads. That is a lookup by id in a served read, not a join on names. The other option: the spec adds an optional `label` to the `nav` arm. The implementer states which one, and why, in the claim. If it is the spec arm, this card waits on a `domain:spec` slice and says so. Either way, the id stays visible as secondary text.
2. **The contributor's empty state tells the truth.** When a served read names what the package contributes, the pillar says so ("Adds 2 entries to Multi-Package Core's app") instead of "no app yet". If no served read names it, the text stops claiming the package has nothing and points to where its entries appear. The implementer measures which reads are available first.
3. Strings go in the studio en and zh packs. No metadata key is added.

**Reader.** `domain:ui`, size S. `Clause-②: no` is expected, unless item 1 lands on a spec arm, which is then a separate spec slice.

**Dedupe.** Searched `contributed nav label`, `no app yet contributes` and `navigationContributions empty state`; the open hits are seat posts and unrelated cards (#23181, #25943), plus the source card #29786. **New.**

Links back: #29786 / PR #29847, ruling 6566915346 (#27928), #28722.
